# Tools: Workspaces, projects and people (+ project kickoff)

Cards for every tool this skill names. Rendered authority: [A] call · [C] confirm first · [O] owner order only.

## Owned

### `create_workspace` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a new workspace (top collaboration boundary) with the caller as owner.
Use when: The user explicitly asks to create a new workspace (new client, area or product line).    Avoid when: A suitable workspace already exists: find it with list_workspaces.; You need a new project inside an existing workspace: use create_project.; You need to add people: use add_workspace_member.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | yes | user | Non-empty after trim. |
| slug | no | user | Derived from name when omitted. Uniqueness is NOT checked. |
| description | no | user |  |
Preconditions: list_workspaces shows no workspace for this purpose.; The user confirmed creation.
Returns: Text 'Workspace created with ID: <workspaceId>'.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Workspace name is required' | Send a non-empty name. |
Gotchas:
- Every call creates another workspace (no dedupe by name or slug): never retry blindly, re-check list_workspaces first. The caller becomes owner.
- No AI config is stored, so the default AI policy applies (AI enabled, default provider and models, server-default budgets).
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_workspace`, `add_workspace_member`, `create_project`

### `update_workspace` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Changes a workspace's name, slug, description or status (active or archived).
Use when: The user asks to rename a workspace or change its description.; The user explicitly asks to archive or reactivate a workspace.    Avoid when: You want to change AI providers, models or budgets: that is update_workspace_ai_config (owner-only).; You want to change members: use add_workspace_member or remove_workspace_member.; You want to change the operating model or context: use apply_workspace_context_update.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id |  |
| name | no | user | Non-empty if sent. |
| slug | no | user | Not validated or checked for uniqueness. |
| description | no | user |  |
| status | no | constant | Only 'active' or 'archived' (the server does not validate it with an API key). |
Preconditions: The workspace exists.; The caller is workspace owner or an active member with role owner/admin (list_workspaces -> access.canManage = true).
Returns: Text 'Workspace <workspaceId> updated successfully.' Only the fields you sent change.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Workspace not found' | Re-read ids with list_workspaces. |
| 'You do not have permission to update this workspace' | Ask the workspace owner or an admin. |
| 'Workspace name is required' | Do not send an empty name. |
Gotchas:
- status='archived' is an archive: ChatGPT/Claude OAuth connectors bound to that workspace start failing with access denied and it disappears from OAuth list_workspaces.
- Treat it as destructive and confirm.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_workspace`

### `create_project` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a new project owned by the caller, with a name and a short key, optionally inside a workspace and a team.
Use when: User explicitly asks to create a new project and gives or approves its name, key and workspace    Avoid when: The project may already exist: check list_projects first (the server does not check name or key uniqueness); You want to bring back an archived project: use unarchive_project; You want new work inside an existing project: use create_issue
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | yes | user | Trimmed; must not be empty. |
| key | yes | user | Short, stable project key (e.g. PROJ). Trimmed and upper-cased by the server. Not checked for uniqueness. |
| description | no | user | Trimmed free text. |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Strongly recommended: the workspace is the main collaboration boundary, and a project without a workspace is unreachable through OAuth connectors. |
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | Optional operational slice; leave empty when the workspace already covers collaboration. |
Preconditions: API key authentication (tool is not offered to OAuth connectors); Caller can read the target workspace and team when given; User confirmed name, key and workspace
Returns: Plain text, not JSON: 'Project created with ID: <projectId>'. Take the ID after 'ID: '.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project name is required / Project key is required | Send a non-empty name and key. |
| You do not have access to the target workspace / target team | Use a workspaceId from list_workspaces or a teamId from list_teams that the caller belongs to. |
| -32003 This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: create_project, or OAuth insufficient_scope | The connection cannot create projects. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Not idempotent: a retry after a timeout creates a duplicate project, so check list_projects by key before retrying.
- The caller becomes ownerId; the project starts with archived=false and no baseline (unbaselined).
- Recommended order after creation (help article 'como-comecar-um-projeto'): governance roles, then baseline and requirements, then issues.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `list_projects`, `get_project`, `update_project`, `create_requirement_baseline`, `create_issue`

### `update_project` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Changes project settings: name, description, archived flag, workspace or team placement, governance role assignments or routing profile.
Use when: User asks to rename the project or edit its description; The owner explicitly instructs to set the project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead assignments; The owner explicitly instructs to move the project to another workspace or team    Avoid when: Only archiving or restoring: use archive_project or unarchive_project; Changing work items: use update_issue, update_cycle or update_milestone; Changing scope or roadmap: use the governed flows (change sets, submit_workspace_roadmap_change), not project settings
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| name | no | user | Trimmed; empty string is rejected. |
| description | no | user | Trimmed. |
| archived | no | constant | Boolean. Prefer archive_project / unarchive_project. |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Moves the project to that workspace and recomputes its routing profile. |
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | Moves the project to that team. |
| governanceAssignments | no | user (userId from list_project_assignable_members -> uid) | Array of {role: project-owner\|product-owner\|delivery-lead, userId}. REPLACES the whole list; one entry per role; userIds starting with 'agent:' are dropped. |
| routingProfile | no | user | Object of string arrays: domains, ownedCapabilities, ownedComponents, ownedSystems, aliases, intakeKeywords, excludedKeywords, escalationRules, maintainedBy. Requires the project to belong to a workspace. |
Preconditions: Caller can manage the project (project owner, project-owner role, workspace manager or team admin); governanceAssignments, routingProfile and workspace/team moves only on explicit owner instruction, because they change who decides; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Project <projectId> updated successfully.' Call get_project to read the new state.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project not found | Wrong projectId; get it from list_projects (includeArchived=true). |
| You do not have permission to update this project | Caller is not a project manager. Stop and tell the user who can do it (get_project -> governanceAssignments). |
| You do not have access to the target workspace / target team | Use a workspace or team the caller belongs to. |
| Project routing profile requires the project to belong to a workspace | Set workspaceId first (owner decision) or drop routingProfile. |
| Hourly rate must be a valid number / Operational curation SLA must be between 1 and 720 hours | You sent an undeclared field; remove it (hourlyRate is a financial decision for the owner). |
Gotchas:
- Every argument except projectId is written into the project document as sent; the server does not reject unknown fields.
- Send ONLY the fields you mean to change and never send fields outside the schema.
- governanceAssignments replaces the full list: read get_project first and resend the roles you keep.
- Records a 'settings updated' activity only when something changed.
Pairs with: `get_project`, `list_project_assignable_members`, `list_workspaces`

### `archive_project` [C] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Sets archived=true on a project so it disappears from active project lists; all data is kept and the change can be undone.
Use when: User asks to archive, close or hide a finished or paused project    Avoid when: Permanent removal: delete_project (owner-only); Restoring: unarchive_project
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller can manage the project; User confirmed the project name; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Project <projectId> archived successfully.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project not found | Wrong projectId; check list_projects with includeArchived=true. |
| You do not have permission to update this project | Caller is not a project manager; tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Only visibility changes: archived projects are hidden from list_projects unless includeArchived=true, but project access checks ignore archived, so reads and writes on their issues still work.
- Reversible with unarchive_project.
Pairs with: `get_project`, `unarchive_project`, `list_projects`

### `unarchive_project` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Sets archived=false on an archived project so it shows again in active project lists.
Use when: User asks to restore or reopen an archived project    Avoid when: Project is not archived (check get_project -> archived): nothing to do; Creating a new project: create_project
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects (includeArchived=true) -> id | Archived projects only appear in list_projects with includeArchived=true. |
Preconditions: Caller can manage the project; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Project <projectId> restored successfully.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project not found | Wrong projectId; list with includeArchived=true. |
| You do not have permission to update this project | Caller is not a project manager; tell the user. |
Gotchas:
- Reverses an earlier archive decision, so confirm with the user.
- It does not restore deleted data: delete_project removes the project recursively and cannot be undone.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_project`, `archive_project`

### `delete_project` [O] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Permanently deletes a project and everything stored under it (issues, comments, cycles, milestones, requirements, baselines, file records, ledger), plus its activity-feed entries and cross-project issue links.
Use when: The owner explicitly orders permanent deletion of this exact project (e.g. a test or duplicate project), after you showed its name and key from get_project    Avoid when: The project is finished, paused or no longer wanted in lists: use archive_project (reversible); Removing one work item: use update_issue status=canceled or delete_issue
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id | Confirm name and key with get_project before calling. |
Preconditions: Caller can manage the project; Explicit owner instruction naming this project; API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Project <projectId> deleted successfully.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found | Already deleted or wrong ID. Check list_projects with includeArchived=true; do not retry blindly. |
| You do not have permission to manage this project | Stop and tell the user; only a project manager can delete. |
Gotchas:
- Irreversible: Firestore recursive delete with no soft delete, no undo and no server-side confirmation step.
- Financial records (ledger transactions) and baselines are destroyed too.
- Uploaded storage objects are not removed by this command.
- Default to archive_project unless the owner insists.
Pairs with: `get_project`, `archive_project`, `list_projects`

Purpose: Lists the members of a workspace with their roles.
Use when: You need the userId, email or role of people in a workspace.; You must confirm the caller is owner/admin before using admin tools.; Choosing accountableOwnerUserId (role owner/admin) for agent principals or credentials.; Before add_workspace_member, to avoid adding someone twice. Returns: JSON array of {id (= userId), workspaceId, userId, userEmail, role (owner|admin|member|viewer), status, createdAt, updatedAt}.

### `add_workspace_member` [C] · write · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Gives an existing LPM user access to a workspace with a role.
Use when: The workspace owner or an admin asks to give a person access to a workspace.    Avoid when: The person is already in list_workspace_members (the call fails).; Changing a role: there is no update tool; remove_workspace_member then add_workspace_member, only after the user confirms.; Grouping inside a workspace: use add_team_member.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document id of the workspace. |
| userId | yes | user, or get_user / list_team_members -> userId / list_project_assignable_members -> uid | The server does not check that it exists or matches userEmail; verify it with get_user first. |
| userEmail | yes | get_user -> email | Stored as given (trimmed, not lowercased). |
| role | yes | constant | enum owner\|admin\|member\|viewer. Least privilege: member or viewer; owner/admin only on explicit instruction of the workspace owner. The server does not validate the value. |
Preconditions: The caller is the workspace owner or an active admin.; The person has an LPM account (get_user returns it).; The person is not already a member.; The API key profile is full or custom.
Returns: Plain text: 'Member <userId> added to workspace <workspaceId>.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have permission to add members to this workspace' | Caller is not owner/admin, or the workspaceId is wrong. Ask the workspace owner. |
| 'User ID is required' / 'User email is required' | Send both userId and userEmail. |
| 'User is already a workspace member' | Nothing to do; confirm the role with list_workspace_members. |
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: <name>' | Sensitive admin tool: only 'full' or 'custom' API keys include it. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user; never try to widen your own key. |
Gotchas:
- No MCP tool finds a user by email: get the userId from the user or from another listing.
- A wrong userId creates a membership for nobody.
- Access to all workspace projects starts immediately.
- No notification is sent to the person.
- An admin can grant 'owner'; that is the owner's decision.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_members`, `get_user`

### `remove_workspace_member` [C] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Removes a person's membership from a workspace, or lets the caller leave it.
Use when: The workspace owner or an admin asks to remove someone.; The caller asks to leave a workspace (memberId = own userId).    Avoid when: Removing the person from a team only: use remove_team_member.; Only changing the role: still remove + add, but only after explicit confirmation.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document id of the workspace. |
| memberId | yes | list_workspace_members -> id | Member document id, equal to the userId. |
Preconditions: The caller is owner/admin, or memberId is the caller.; The target appears in list_workspace_members.; The target is not the workspace owner and not the last owner/admin (the server does not check).
Returns: Plain text: 'Member <memberId> removed from workspace <workspaceId>.' It is returned even if the person was not a member.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have permission to remove members from this workspace' | Caller is not owner/admin. Ask the workspace owner. |
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: <name>' | Sensitive admin tool: only 'full' or 'custom' API keys include it. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user; never try to widen your own key. |
Gotchas:
- No safety checks: it can remove admins or the owner's member record (the owner keeps access through the workspace ownerId).
- If the removed person is accountableOwnerUserId of owner-agent credentials, those credentials stop working at once.
- The person may still reach projects through team membership.
- Their activities stay assigned to them.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_members`, `list_workspace_mcp_agent_credentials`

### `get_user` [A] · read · KEY · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Reads one user's profile by user id.
Use when: Verifying that a userId exists, and getting its email, before add_workspace_member or add_team_member.; Showing the name/email behind an assigneeId, creatorId, ownerId or accountableOwnerUserId.    Avoid when: Finding a user by email: no MCP tool does this; ask the user for the id or look in list_workspace_members.; Assignee candidates for a project: use list_project_assignable_members.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| userId | yes | list_workspace_members -> userId, list_team_members -> userId, list_project_assignable_members -> uid, or an id field on issues/projects | Firebase uid. |
Preconditions: userId is a real LPM user id.
Returns: JSON profile document {id, uid, email, displayName, photoURL, role, language, and hourlyRate/currency/theme if set}. Users without a profile document return {uid, email, displayName, photoURL, role:'user'} (no id field).
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 'User not found' | Wrong id; re-read it from list_workspace_members or ask the user. |
Gotchas:
- No access check: returns any user's profile, including email and hourlyRate.
- Treat it as personal data; never paste it into comments or shared channels.
- To learn your own userId: list_api_keys -> userId, or your row in list_workspace_members.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.

Purpose: Adds an existing LPM user to a team with a role and sends them an in-app notification.
Use when: A team owner/admin asks to add a person to a team.    Avoid when: Giving access to a workspace: use add_workspace_member (the workspace is the primary boundary).; The person is already in list_team_members (the call fails).; Changing an existing member's role: there is no update tool; remove_team_member then add_team_member, only after the user confirms.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| teamId | yes | list_teams -> id |  |
| userId | yes | list_workspace_members -> userId, list_project_assignable_members -> uid, or user | Required by the schema. The server stores it as given and does not check it matches userEmail; verify it with get_user first. |
| userEmail | yes | get_user -> email | Lowercased by the server. |
| role | yes | constant | enum owner\|admin\|member. Use member unless the team owner explicitly asks for owner/admin. The server does not validate the value. |
Preconditions: The caller is the team owner or an active team member with role owner/admin.; The person has an LPM account (get_user returns it).; The person is not already a member (list_team_members).
Returns: Plain text: 'Member <userId> added to team <teamId>.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have permission to manage this team' | The caller is not owner/admin of the team, or the teamId does not exist. Check with get_team and list_team_members; ask the team owner. |
| 'User is already a team member' | Nothing to do; confirm the role with list_team_members. Do not retry. |
| 'User not found' | No LPM account for that id/email. Ask the person to sign up first. |
| 'Member email is required' | Send userEmail. |
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: <name>' | Sensitive admin tool: only 'full' or 'custom' API keys include it. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user; never try to widen your own key. |
Gotchas:
- Membership gives read access to every project whose teamId is this team.
- Creates an in-app 'Team invitation' notification for the person (outward-facing).
- When userId and userEmail are both sent they are stored without cross-checking; with only userEmail the server looks the user up by email.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Pairs with: `list_teams`, `list_team_members`, `get_user`

### `remove_team_member` [C] · destructive · KEY · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Removes one person from a team.
Use when: A team owner/admin asks to remove a person from a team.    Avoid when: Removing the person from a workspace: use remove_workspace_member.; Deleting the whole team: use delete_team.; The person is the team owner: the server refuses.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| teamId | yes | list_teams -> id |  |
| memberId | yes | list_team_members -> id | Member document id, equal to the person's userId. |
Preconditions: The caller is the team owner or an active team admin.; memberId is a current member and is not the team's ownerId.
Returns: Plain text: 'Member <memberId> removed from team <teamId>.'
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'You do not have permission to manage this team' | Caller is not owner/admin, or the teamId does not exist. Ask the team owner. |
| 'Team owner cannot be removed' | Stop. Ownership transfer is not supported through MCP; tell the user. |
| 'Team member not found' | Already removed or wrong id; re-check with list_team_members. |
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: <name>' | Sensitive admin tool: only 'full' or 'custom' API keys include it. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user; never try to widen your own key. |
Gotchas:
- Access to the team's projects ends at once, unless the person also reaches them through workspace membership.
- Their assigned activities are not reassigned.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Pairs with: `list_team_members`

## Used here (owned by another skill; rules live there)

### `list_workspaces` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the workspaces the caller can reach, to obtain workspaceId.
Use when: First step of almost any task: find the workspaceId by name.; Checking whether you can manage a workspace (API key: access.canManage).    Avoid when: You already have the workspaceId and need its details: use get_workspace.; You need the projects: use list_workspace_projects or list_projects.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | API key only; OAuth rejects it as unknown_field. |
| status | no | constant | active \| archived. |
| compact | no | constant | true returns only id, name, key, status, teamId, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt (drops access.canManage). |
| limit | no | constant | Max number returned. OAuth: integer 1-100. |
Preconditions: OAuth: scope workspace:read.
Returns: API key: array (newest first) of workspace records {id, name, slug, description, status, ownerId, teamId, createdAt, updatedAt, access:{canManage}}. OAuth: [{id, name}] of authorized active workspaces only.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| OAuth -32602 invalid_arguments (unknown_field teamId, or limit out of range) | Under OAuth send only status, compact, limit (1-100). |
| -32003 access denied | Call get_mcp_connection_info to see the connection's scopes. |
Gotchas:
- access.canManage=true (owner/admin) is required for update_workspace, delete_workspace_issue_link and update_workspace_ai_config.
- With an API key the list also includes workspaces where you only own a project; get_workspace may then deny access.
- OAuth: status 'archived' always returns [] and a single-workspace grant returns only that workspace.
- Use compact:true to save context only when you do not need canManage.
Pairs with: `get_mcp_connection_info`, `get_workspace`, `list_workspace_projects`

### `get_workspace` [A] · read · workspace:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns the stored record of one workspace (name, slug, status, owner, dates).
Use when: Confirming a workspaceId and reading its name and status before acting.    Avoid when: You need a richer summary: use get_workspace_read_model or get_workspace_executive_context.; You need its projects: use list_workspace_projects. Members: list_workspace_members. AI settings: get_workspace_ai_config.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id |  |
Preconditions: The workspace exists.; The caller is the owner or an active member; OAuth: scope workspace:read and the workspace is in the grant.
Returns: {id, name, slug, description, ownerId, status, createdAt, updatedAt, plus any other stored fields}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 'Workspace not found' | Re-read ids with list_workspaces. |
| -32602 'You do not have access to this workspace' | You are not a member. Ask the owner to add you; do not guess another id. |
| OAuth -32003 not authorized | The workspace is outside the connector's grant. Call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Raw record: it does not tell your role; use list_workspaces access.canManage for that.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `list_workspace_projects`

### `list_projects` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the projects the caller can see (as owner, workspace member or team member), optionally filtered by workspace or team; archived projects are hidden unless includeArchived=true.
Use when: You need a projectId and only know the project name or key; User asks which projects exist in a workspace or team; Start of a session, to pick the project to work on    Avoid when: You already have the projectId: use get_project; You need the open work of a project: use get_project_execution_context; You need the workspace view of its projects with workspace context: list_workspace_projects is equivalent for one workspace
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Optional with an API key but REQUIRED under OAuth (ChatGPT/Claude connectors). With a workspace agent credential it defaults to the credential's workspace and any other value is rejected. |
| teamId | no | list_teams -> id | Exact-match filter. |
| includeArchived | no | constant | Boolean, default false. Set true to find archived projects (e.g. before unarchive_project). |
Preconditions: Under OAuth the workspaceId must be a workspace included in the grant
Returns: JSON array of full project documents: id, name, key, description, ownerId, workspaceId, teamId, archived, createdAt and, when set, governanceAssignments, routingProfile, hourlyRate. Use id as projectId in every project-scoped tool.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 This project listing requires an explicit workspaceId. (OAuth) | Call list_workspaces, take the id of the right workspace, retry with workspaceId. |
| -32003 The requested resource is outside the credential scope | You passed a workspaceId other than the agent credential's workspace; omit workspaceId. |
| Empty array | Check workspaceId/teamId, retry with includeArchived=true; if still empty the caller has no access. Ask the user; never guess IDs. |
Gotchas:
- No pagination: returns every matching project.
- A project where the caller only holds a governance role (not owner, not workspace/team member) is NOT listed, although get_project works for it.
- Without workspaceId (API key) the server scans all projects, so pass workspaceId when known.
- Match the user's project by name or key; never guess an ID.
Pairs with: `list_workspaces`, `get_project`, `get_project_execution_context`, `list_issues`
CLI: `lpm projects list [--workspace-id <id>] [--team-id <id>] [--include-archived] [--json]`

### `get_project` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-start` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, roadmap-owner-advisor, roadmap-owner-operator, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns one project's settings with its resolved governance roles and whether the caller can manage it.
Use when: Verify a projectId and show its name/key before acting; Find who holds project-owner, product-owner and delivery-lead roles (who to escalate to); Check access.canManage before tools that need manage rights (update_project, archive_project, create_project_file, delete_project_file)    Avoid when: You need open issues, decisions and scope gate: use get_project_execution_context; You need the executive summary only: use get_project_owner_surface; You do not know the projectId yet: use list_projects
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: JSON project: id, name, key, description, ownerId, workspaceId, teamId, archived, createdAt, governanceAssignments [{role, userId, source}] (resolved), routingProfile, plus access {canManage: boolean}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found | Wrong ID; get it from list_projects. |
| You do not have access to this project | Caller cannot read it; ask the user for access, do not retry. |
| -32003 (OAuth) not authorized | Project is outside the granted workspace or has no workspace; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Cheap call: one project document read plus a permission check (access.canManage).
- Holding a governance role is authority to decide; being an issue assignee is not.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_project_execution_context`, `update_project`
CLI: `lpm project get <projectId> [--json]`

### `list_unowned_domains_or_capabilities` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-executive-context` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns only the ownership-coverage gaps: executive-context domains and capabilities that no project claims, plus projects whose routing profile points to another workspace.
Use when: Before routing intake, to see which areas have no owning project; validate_workspace_project_alignment reported warnings or blockers and you need the individual items    Avoid when: All gap types -> list_workspace_context_gaps; Only a status/score for alignment -> validate_workspace_project_alignment; Roadmap capability records (ids, owners, tags) -> list_workspace_capabilities
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | yes | list_workspaces -> id | Firestore document ID. |
Preconditions: Caller is the workspace owner or an active workspace member; API key access: not exposed to OAuth connectors
Returns: {workspace, executiveContext, generatedAt, unownedDomains[gap], unownedCapabilities[gap], alignmentIssues[gap]} where each gap is {id, gapType, severity, title, detail, evidence[], suggestedAction, requiresHumanConfirmation} as in list_workspace_context_gaps.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| You do not have access to this workspace | Re-check the ID with list_workspaces; the caller must be the owner or an active member. |
| Tool not listed or -32003 on an OAuth connector | Needs an LPM API key; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- 'Capabilities' here are executive-context strings matched against project routingProfile.ownedCapabilities, not roadmap capability records.
- A domain or capability counts as owned when at least one non-archived project's routingProfile lists it (routingProfile.domains / routingProfile.ownedCapabilities).
- Fix by claiming it on the right project with update_project routingProfile (confirm with the user), or by removing it from the context with apply_workspace_context_update portfolio.domains/capabilities (owner-only; that list is replaced, not merged).
- Strings that come from a project's routing profile cannot be removed through the context.
- alignmentIssues usually means a project's routingProfile.workspaceId is stale: re-save the routingProfile with update_project.
Pairs with: `list_workspace_projects`, `update_project`, `validate_workspace_project_alignment`

### `create_export_request` [O] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-integrations` · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Queues a background job that packages all data of a workspace or of one project into a JSON zip for download in the LPM web app.
Use when: The user explicitly asks for a backup or full data export of a workspace or project.    Avoid when: You only need some records: use the matching list_/get_ tools.; You need analytics: use get_project_analytics or get_operational_analytics.; An export for the same scope is already queued or running (check list_export_requests).
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| scope | yes | constant | workspace \| project |
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Required when scope = workspace. |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Required when scope = project. |
| filters | no | user | Object; stored but currently ignored (the export is always complete). |
Preconditions: scope workspace: caller is the workspace owner or an active member.; scope project: caller can read the project.; API key profile includes sensitive admin tools (full or custom).; The user explicitly asked for the export.
Returns: Export request object {id, status: 'queued', scope, workspaceId, projectId, format: 'json-zip', createdAt, ...}. Track it with list_export_requests.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Workspace export requires a workspace' | Pass workspaceId with scope workspace. |
| 'Project export requires a project' | Pass projectId with scope project. |
| 'You do not have access to this workspace' | The caller is not an active member. Ask the workspace owner. |
| 'Project <id> not found' / 'You do not have access to this project' | Check projectId with list_projects; ask for access if needed. |
Gotchas:
- Asynchronous: poll list_export_requests until status is completed or failed.
- On completion the requester gets a notification ('Export concluído') and webhooks subscribed to export.completed fire.
- The zip holds ALL data of the scope (flagged in the catalog as a data exfiltration risk); filters are stored but ignored by the export job.
- Each call queues a new full export.
- No download link via MCP: the user downloads it from LPM Settings.
Pairs with: `list_export_requests`, `list_notifications`

### `list_requirement_baselines` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, read-only, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists all requirement baselines (approved scope snapshots) of a project, newest first; the one with isCurrent=true is the approved scope.
Use when: You need a baselineId for list_requirements or create_requirement (take the item with isCurrent=true); Checking baseline history and version names before a publication    Avoid when: You need delta counts or publication gate - use get_project_scope_resolution_context (it also returns currentBaseline)
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
Preconditions: Project exists and the caller can read it
Returns: Array of {id, name, version, description, isCurrent, publishedAt, publishedBy, previousBaselineId, previousBaselineName, publicationNotes, changeSetId, contentFingerprint, requirementCount, createdAt}. Pick isCurrent=true.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Empty array | Wrong projectId or the project has no baseline yet; verify with get_project. The first baseline is published with publish_baseline_from_working_scope on the owner's instruction. |
| -32003 access denied by OAuth policy, or OPERATION_FAILED under an OAuth connector | Call get_mcp_connection_info to check the portfolio:read scope; OAuth hides domain error text, so retry once and then report the projectId you used. |
Gotchas:
- Not paginated.
- If no item has isCurrent=true the project is unbaselined (risk scope:no-current-baseline).
- Each baseline holds its own copies of requirements; never edit requirements of a non-current baseline unless told to.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `list_requirements`, `create_requirement`, `get_project_scope_resolution_context`

### `list_issues` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-deliver-activity` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the issues (activities) of one project, optionally filtered by status, priority, assignee, cycle or milestone, with optional cursor pagination.
Use when: You need issue IDs (e.g. for update_issue, comments, or the commit trailer 'LPM-Activity: <id>'); User asks for the backlog, the work in progress, or the issues of a cycle, milestone or person    Avoid when: You need one known issue: use get_issue; You need overdue, unassigned, unestimated or blocked issues: use list_overdue_project_issues, list_unassigned_project_issues, list_unestimated_project_issues or list_blocked_project_issues; You need the prioritized open work with context: use get_project_execution_context
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| status | no | constant | backlog \| todo \| in-progress \| done \| canceled (exact match). |
| priority | no | constant | none \| low \| medium \| high \| urgent. |
| assigneeId | no | list_project_assignable_members -> uid |  |
| cycleId | no | list_cycles -> id |  |
| milestoneId | no | list_milestones -> id |  |
| cursor | no | list_issues -> nextCursor | Only valid with the SAME projectId and filters that produced it. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Integer 1-100. Passing it switches the response to the paginated shape. |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: Without cursor/limitCount: a JSON array of ALL matching issues. With cursor or limitCount: {items, nextCursor, hasMore}. Each issue: id, title, description, status, priority, assigneeId, cycleId, milestoneId, estimate, dueDate, labelIds, requirementId, baselineId, startedAt, completedAt, actualHours, createdAt, updatedAt.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Invalid OAuth tool arguments / 'OAuth grant does not permit this operation or resource.' on a paginated call | Bad cursor or limitCount: restart without cursor, keep the same filters, use an integer limitCount 1-100. |
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Check projectId with list_projects; ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- Always pass limitCount (e.g. 50) on big projects: without it the whole project is returned in one response.
- Loop while hasMore is true, passing nextCursor.
- Filters are exact matches and combine with AND.
- The issue id is the value for the commit trailer 'LPM-Activity: <id>'.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_issue`, `update_issue`, `create_comment`
CLI: `lpm issues list --project <projectId> [--status <status>] [--priority <priority>] [--assignee <userId>] [--cycle <cycleId>] [--milestone <milestoneId>] [--json]`

### `get_project_execution_context` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns the agent-oriented working context of a project: owner view, top open issues, active cycles, open milestones, decision inbox, scope/baseline publication gate and change sets.
Use when: First call when you start working on a project: what is open, what is blocked on decisions, what to do next; User asks 'what should we work on now' for a project; Before proposing scope changes, to see the current baseline, working scope delta and publication gate    Avoid when: You only need issues with filters or more than 50 open issues: use list_issues; You only need the executive summary: use get_project_owner_surface; You need decisions only: use get_project_decision_inbox
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project AND holds a project governance role (project-owner, product-owner or delivery-lead; the ownerId counts): the tool reads the project decision inbox, which reads the owner surface; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: {project, generatedAt, ownerView, planning:{openIssues (max 50, not done/canceled, urgent first), activeCycles (status=active), openMilestones (status!=closed), nextRecommendedActivity}, governance (decision inbox, up to 20), scope:{currentBaseline, workingScope, delta, publicationGate}, changeSets:{totalCount, activeCount, items (first 20)}}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Check projectId with list_projects; ask the user for access. |
| -32003 (OAuth) not authorized | Project outside the grant or without a workspace; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
| You do not have access to this owner surface | The caller has no project governance role; use get_project_read_model or list_issues instead, or ask the owner to assign a role. |
Gotchas:
- Built on get_project_read_model, so it is heavy and has the same API-key side effect (orphan requirements re-pointed to the current baseline).
- openIssues is capped at 50; use list_issues for the rest.
- Decisions listed in governance belong to the owner: present them, do not decide them.
- With an API key and grounding enabled, the owner-surface step may run a document search that spends the daily grounding quota: do not call it in a loop.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_issue`, `list_issues`, `update_issue`, `get_project_decision_inbox`

### `create_cycle` [A] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, planning, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a cycle (sprint) with a name, a start and an end date in a project; status starts as 'upcoming' unless given.
Use when: User asks to open a new sprint or execution window with given dates    Avoid when: A cycle for that window already exists: check list_cycles, then update_cycle; You need a value checkpoint or delivery commitment: use create_milestone
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| name | yes | user | Not validated server-side; always send a non-empty name. |
| startDate | yes | user | ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. Not validated; always send it (cycles without startDate vanish from read models). |
| endDate | yes | user | ISO date YYYY-MM-DD, after startDate (not checked by the server). |
| status | no | constant | upcoming \| active \| completed. Default upcoming. Not validated with an API key: copy exactly. |
| assigneeId | no | list_project_assignable_members -> uid | Not checked for eligibility; use only an eligible uid. |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project (read access is enough); API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Cycle created with ID: <cycleId>'.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Check projectId with list_projects; ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- Not idempotent: a retry creates a second cycle; check list_cycles before retrying.
- The server stores the arguments as sent (no validation of dates, status or name), so the agent must validate them.
- Assign issues afterwards with update_issue cycleId.
Pairs with: `list_cycles`, `list_project_assignable_members`, `update_issue`, `get_cycle`

### `list_milestones` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists all milestones (value checkpoints / delivery commitments) of a project.
Use when: You need a milestoneId (for create_issue, update_issue, list_issues filter, update_milestone); User asks which milestones exist or which are still open    Avoid when: You only need open milestones with open work: get_project_execution_context -> planning.openMilestones; You know the milestoneId: use get_milestone
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller should have read access to the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: JSON array of milestones: id, name, description, targetDate, status (open|closed), assigneeId, requirementId, baselineId, projectId, workspaceId, createdAt.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Empty array | The project has no milestones (or the projectId is wrong); verify with get_project. |
| -32003 (OAuth) not authorized | Project outside the grant or without a workspace; call get_mcp_connection_info. |
Gotchas:
- Unsorted and unpaginated; sort by targetDate yourself.
- To get a milestone's issues call list_issues with milestoneId.
Pairs with: `list_projects`, `get_milestone`, `list_issues`, `create_milestone`, `update_issue`

### `create_milestone` [A] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, planning, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a milestone (checkpoint of value or delivery commitment) with a name and target date in a project; status starts as 'open'.
Use when: User asks to register a delivery checkpoint or commitment date that groups several issues or cycles    Avoid when: You need a time-boxed execution window: use create_cycle; A milestone for that checkpoint already exists: check list_milestones, then update_milestone; It is a roadmap-level outcome across projects: use the workspace roadmap tools
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| name | yes | user | Not validated server-side; always send a non-empty name. |
| description | no | user |  |
| targetDate | yes | user | ISO date YYYY-MM-DD. Not validated; always send it (milestones without targetDate vanish from read models). |
| status | no | constant | open \| closed. Default open. Not validated with an API key: copy exactly. |
| assigneeId | no | list_project_assignable_members -> uid | Not checked for eligibility; use only an eligible uid. |
Preconditions: Caller can read the project (read access is enough); The target date was given or approved by the user (a milestone is a commitment); API key authentication (not offered to OAuth connectors)
Returns: Plain text: 'Milestone created with ID: <milestoneId>'.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Check projectId with list_projects; ask the user for access. |
Gotchas:
- Not idempotent: a retry creates a duplicate; check list_milestones before retrying.
- Arguments are stored as sent with no validation.
- Attach issues afterwards with update_issue milestoneId.
Pairs with: `list_milestones`, `list_project_assignable_members`, `update_issue`, `get_milestone`

### `list_labels` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists every universal label (id, name, color); labels are shared by all LPM workspaces.
Use when: Before setting labelIds on create_issue or update_issue.; Before create_label, to reuse an existing label instead of duplicating it.; Translating labelIds found on activities into names.    Avoid when: You want labels of one project or workspace only: there is no such scope; filter mentally from this global list.
Preconditions: Authenticated API key whose profile includes the tool.
Returns: JSON array sorted by name: {id, name, color, createdAt, updatedAt?}. Use id inside labelIds.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: list_labels' | Call get_mcp_connection_info and ask the owner for a profile that includes it. |
Gotchas:
- Global catalog, no workspace filter, no pagination.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors: ChatGPT/Claude can send labelIds on create_issue/update_issue but cannot list labels.
Pairs with: `create_issue`, `update_issue`

### `create_label` [C] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, planning, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a new universal label that every LPM workspace will see.
Use when: The user explicitly asks for a new label and list_labels has no label with that meaning.    Avoid when: A label with the same or similar name exists: reuse its id from list_labels.; You only want to describe one activity: put it in the description or a create_comment.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | yes | user | Trimmed; 1-99 characters. |
| color | yes | user or constant | Exactly '#RRGGBB' (6 hex digits). Short form like '#fff' is rejected. |
Preconditions: No equivalent label exists (the server does not check duplicates).; The user approved creating a platform-wide label.
Returns: Text 'Label created with ID: <labelId>'. Use labelId in labelIds of create_issue/update_issue.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| 'Label name is required' / 'Label name must be shorter than 100 characters' | Send a non-empty name under 100 chars. |
| 'Label color must be a valid hex code' | Use '#RRGGBB', e.g. '#1f77b4'. |
Gotchas:
- Labels are global: no workspace/tenant scoping and no permission check beyond being signed in, so every customer sees the new label.
- Duplicate names are allowed; a retry creates a second label.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `list_labels`, `update_issue`

### `create_project_repository_link` [C] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-code-index` · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Attach a GitHub repository (read-only) to one project so it can be scanned for metadata and shown to agents.
Use when: The user asks to link a GitHub repository to a specific project; A project has no repository link and the user confirmed which repository (and branch) to use    Avoid when: The repository is already linked to the project (check list_project_repository_links first): use update_project_repository_link; You need code search, code index or exact excerpts for the repository: use create_workspace_repository_link with projectMappings (project links are never code-indexed); One repository serves several projects (umbrella/monorepo): use create_workspace_repository_link with projectMappings
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id | Project must belong to a workspace |
| repositoryUrl | yes | user | Exactly https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> (a trailing .git is stripped). No query, fragment, credentials, IP or non-github.com host. Stored lowercased as canonicalRepositoryUrl |
| defaultBranch | no | user | Branch name; omitted = repository default branch discovered by the scan |
| allowedBranches | no | user | Array of branch names matching [A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,200}; invalid entries are silently dropped; empty = any branch |
| agentVisible | no | constant | boolean, default true; false hides the link from get_project_repository_context and automated scans |
| analysisPolicy | no | constant | metadata_only (default) \| shallow_tree (adds top-level tree and up to 8 manifest summaries, depth <= 2). full_scan is rejected |
| repositoryRole | no | user | primary (default) \| umbrella \| component \| infra \| docs \| legacy |
| componentName | no | user | free text |
| submodulePath | no | user | relative path [A-Za-z0-9._/-]{1,300}; no leading / and no .. |
| relationship | no | user | implements \| composes \| supports \| deploys \| documents \| observes |
| automatedScanEnabled | no | user | boolean, default false; true lets the scheduler re-scan automatically with the creator's stored personal GitHub credential |
| automatedScanIntervalHours | no | user | integer 1..168, default 24 |
Preconditions: Project exists and belongs to a workspace; Caller can manage the project (project owner, project-owner governance role, workspace owner/admin, or team manager); No active link to the same canonical URL exists in this project; User asked for or confirmed the link
Returns: The new link: id (use as repositoryLinkId), canonicalRepositoryUrl, owner, repo, lastScanStatus='never_scanned', visibility='unknown', credentialOwnerId (= caller), automatedScanPolicy.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| An active project repository link already exists for this repository. | Do not retry. Get its id from list_project_repository_links; use update_project_repository_link if something must change. |
| Project repository URL must ... (have the shape https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> / use https / host must be github.com / not include query strings or fragments / not include credentials) | Ask the user for the plain https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> URL. |
| Project repository links require the project to belong to a workspace. | Stop; the project has no workspace. Tell the user. |
| You do not have permission to manage this project | Ask a project owner or workspace owner/admin to do it. |
| Project repository automated scan interval must be an integer from 1 to 168 hours. | Send an integer 1..168 or omit it (default 24). |
| Invalid project repository analysis policy / role / relationship, or full_scan is disabled | Use only the enum values listed in inputs. |
Gotchas:
- The caller becomes credentialOwnerId: private-repository scans (manual and automated) fall back to the caller's personal GitHub credential.
- Creating does not scan; call scan_project_repository_readonly next.
- Audited (project_repository_link_created).
- API key only (not in OAuth connectors).
Pairs with: `list_project_repository_links`, `scan_project_repository_readonly`, `get_project_repository_context`
CLI: `lpm project-repos create --project <projectId> --url <github-url> [--branch <branch>] [--allowed-branches <b1; b2>] [--analysis-policy <metadata_only|shallow_tree>] [--role <primary|umbrella|component|infra|docs|legacy>] [--component <name>] [--submodule-path <path>] [--relationship <implements|composes|supports|deploys|documents|observes>] [--automated-scan-enabled] [--automated-scan-interval-hours <1..168>] [--agent-hidden] [--json]`

### `scan_project_repository_readonly` [A] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-code-index` · profiles: full, portfolio, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Read GitHub metadata (branch head commit, languages, default branch, optional shallow tree and manifests) for a project link and store a scan summary.
Use when: The latest scan is missing, failed, or older than 24 h (stale) and you need current repository facts; Before stating anything about the repository's current branch, commit or languages; Right after create_project_repository_link    Avoid when: You need code content or symbol search: use search_project_code / read_repository_file_excerpt (they read the code index, not scans); A scan younger than 24 h exists: read it with get_project_repository_context; Workspace-level links: use scan_workspace_repository_readonly
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id | Project that owns the link |
| repositoryLinkId | yes | list_project_repository_links -> id | Project link id |
| branch | no | user or list_project_repository_links -> defaultBranch | Must be in allowedBranches when that list is non-empty; default = link defaultBranch, then repository default |
| credentialSource | no | constant | default (or omit) \| workspace. 'workspace' uses the workspace GitHub vault; send it only when a workspace owner/admin explicitly asks. Refused for owner-agent credentials |
Preconditions: Link exists in this project and is not archived; Caller can manage the project (scanning needs manage, not read); Workspace used fewer than 10 scans in the last hour (project, workspace and automated scans share this limit); Private repository: the link's credential owner has a personal GitHub credential, or the GitHub App connector is configured, or credentialSource=workspace with a configured vault
Returns: Scan summary: id, status='completed', branch, commitSha (full SHA), visibility (public|private), scannedAt, metadata{description, language, languages, topics, defaultBranch, license, readmePresent}, tree (shallow_tree only: totalEntries, truncated, topLevel[], manifests[{path, summary}]), credentialSource, requestCount. Also updates the link's lastKnownCommit, lastScanAt, lastScanStatus.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Project repository scan rate limit exceeded: max 10 scans per workspace hour. | Stop. Wait up to one hour; never retry in a loop. |
| Requested branch is not allowed for this repository link. | Omit branch or use one listed in allowedBranches. |
| Private or non-public GitHub repositories require a user GitHub credential with read access or a configured read-only GitHub App connector ... | Tell the user: the link owner must configure a personal GitHub credential, or the GitHub App must be installed; a workspace owner/admin may instead rerun with credentialSource=workspace. |
| Private GitHub repository scan failed. Verify the linked user GitHub credential or the read-only GitHub App installation ... | The configured credential or App lacks access to this repository; report to the user. |
| Workspace credential access requires an explicit manager scan. | You are using an owner-agent credential; omit credentialSource. |
| Workspace GitHub credential unavailable or access denied. | Check get_workspace_repository_credential (configured=true) and that the caller is workspace owner/admin; otherwise omit credentialSource. |
| GitHub branch commit SHA could not be resolved. | The branch does not exist; omit branch to use the default. |
| Archived project repository links cannot be scanned. | Use an active link from list_project_repository_links. |
Gotchas:
- A failed scan is still stored (status failed or rate_limited), updates lastScanStatus and counts toward the 10/hour limit, then the call returns an error.
- Limits per scan: 30 s, 30 GitHub requests, 5 MB.
- The tool description says 'public' but private repositories work with a credential.
- A scan never refreshes the code index.
- Manifest summaries redact emails and key=value secrets.
- Owner-agent credentials cannot use stored personal or workspace GitHub credentials (public repos or GitHub App only).
Pairs with: `list_project_repository_links`, `get_project_repository_context`
CLI: `lpm project-repos scan --project <projectId> --link <repositoryLinkId> [--branch <branch>] [--credential-source <default|workspace>] [--json]`

### `create_requirement_baseline` [O] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates a new EMPTY baseline record (optionally marked current); it does not copy any existing requirements.
Use when: The owner explicitly asks for a new empty baseline to be filled manually    Avoid when: Snapshotting the current scope as a new version - use publish_baseline_from_working_scope (clones the current baseline's requirements); Switching which existing baseline is current - use update_requirement_baseline; Agent-proposed scope changes - use create_change_set or create_project_change_set_from_resolution
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
| name | yes | user | free text, e.g. 'Escopo Q4' |
| version | yes | user | free text, e.g. 'v3.0'; duplicates are NOT rejected - check list_requirement_baselines |
| description | no | user | free text |
| isCurrent | no | user | boolean, default false; true demotes the current baseline and runs the publication gate |
Preconditions: The owner explicitly instructed this (baselines are the approved scope - GOV-MAX); Caller can read the project (the server checks only read access); If isCurrent=true and the working-scope delta is medium/high materiality, an approved change set matching the current delta must exist
Returns: Plain text 'Baseline created with ID: <id>' - parse the id after 'ID: '.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Material baseline publication requires an approved change set for the current working scope | Working-scope delta is medium/high materiality. Run create_project_change_set_from_resolution, move it to in-review, wait for the owner's approval, then publish again WITHOUT editing requirements in between (any edit makes the approved snapshot stale). |
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Re-check projectId with list_projects; the caller must belong to the project's workspace or team. |
| -32003 (tool not allowed for this API key/connection, or 'The requested resource is outside the credential scope') | Call get_mcp_connection_info. This tool is not exposed to OAuth connectors; use an API key or agent credential whose profile includes it, on a project of the credential's workspace. |
Gotchas:
- With isCurrent=true the new current baseline starts EMPTY (requirements are copied only with cloneFromBaselineId, which this tool does not declare), so the approved scope shows zero requirements.
- Every requirement with an empty baselineId is attached to the new baseline.
- If the gate matches an approved change set, that change set is auto-marked published.
- Each call creates another baseline.
Pairs with: `list_requirement_baselines`, `create_requirement`, `update_requirement_baseline`

### `update_requirement_baseline` [O] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Edits a baseline's name, version or description, or makes it the current baseline (demoting the previous current one).
Use when: The owner asks to rename or re-describe a baseline; The owner asks to restore an earlier baseline as the current approved scope    Avoid when: Publishing new scope - use publish_baseline_from_working_scope; Editing requirements - use update_requirement
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
| baselineId | yes | list_requirement_baselines -> id |  |
| name | no | user | free text |
| version | no | user | free text |
| description | no | user | free text |
| isCurrent | no | user | send true to promote; never send false (it leaves the project with no current baseline) |
Preconditions: The owner explicitly instructed this change; Baseline exists in the project; Promoting a non-current baseline while the working-scope delta is medium/high materiality requires a matching approved change set
Returns: Plain text 'Baseline <id> updated successfully.' - confirm with list_requirement_baselines.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Baseline not found | Wrong baselineId; re-list with list_requirement_baselines. |
| Material baseline publication requires an approved change set for the current working scope | Working-scope delta is medium/high materiality. Run create_project_change_set_from_resolution, move it to in-review, wait for the owner's approval, then publish again WITHOUT editing requirements in between (any edit makes the approved snapshot stale). |
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Re-check projectId with list_projects; the caller must belong to the project's workspace or team. |
| -32003 (tool not allowed for this API key/connection, or 'The requested resource is outside the credential scope') | Call get_mcp_connection_info. This tool is not exposed to OAuth connectors; use an API key or agent credential whose profile includes it, on a project of the credential's workspace. |
Gotchas:
- Every key you send is written to the baseline as-is (no whitelist) - send only fields you mean to change.
- isCurrent=false on the current baseline is accepted and leaves no current baseline.
- Promoting does not re-point issues; the promoted baseline keeps its own requirement copies.
Pairs with: `list_requirement_baselines`, `get_project_scope_resolution_context`

### `create_requirement` [C] · write · KEY · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: not idempotent
Purpose: Creates one requirement directly in the live scope of a baseline.
Use when: The user/owner explicitly asked to add this requirement to the working scope; Materializing a requirement the owner approved in a governance thread (draft_requirement_from_governance_thread output)    Avoid when: Proposing scope for owner review without touching live scope - use create_governance_thread or create_change_set with requirementProposal; Tracking work to do - use create_issue (requirements are scope, issues are work)
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
| baselineId | yes | list_requirement_baselines -> id (the isCurrent one) | a non-current baseline is accepted but invisible to the working-scope delta |
| title | yes | user | short statement |
| description | yes | user | testable statement / acceptance intent |
| type | yes | constant | functional\|non-functional\|interface\|business\|technical (not validated server-side: use exactly) |
| status | yes | constant | pending\|met\|not-met\|in-progress\|obsolete; use 'pending' for new scope |
| groupId | no | list_requirement_groups -> id |  |
| sourceDocumentId | no | list_project_knowledge_items -> id | not validated |
| issueId | no | list_issues -> id | primary linked issue |
| linkedIssueIds | no | list_issues -> id | array of issue ids |
| linkedCycleIds | no | list_cycles -> id | array; a cycle can belong to only one requirement |
| linkedMilestoneIds | no | list_milestones -> id | array |
Preconditions: The user/owner asked for this scope change (GOV-MAX); otherwise propose it instead; Baseline exists (use the current one); Linked issues/cycles/milestones exist, are not deleted and have no different baselineId
Returns: Plain text 'Requirement created with ID: <id>' - parse the id after 'ID: '.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Baseline is required / Baseline not found | Pass the isCurrent id from list_requirement_baselines. |
| Requirement group not found | Use an id from list_requirement_groups or omit groupId. |
| Linked issue\|cycle\|milestone not found | Verify ids with list_issues / list_cycles / list_milestones (same project, not deleted). |
| Linked issue\|cycle\|milestone does not belong to the selected baseline | That work item is bound to another baseline; link only work items of this baseline or omit. |
| Linked cycle is already associated with another requirement | Cycles are exclusive; unlink it from the other requirement (update_requirement) or omit. |
| Project <id> not found / You do not have access to this project | Re-check projectId with list_projects; the caller must belong to the project's workspace or team. |
| -32003 (tool not allowed for this API key/connection, or 'The requested resource is outside the credential scope') | Call get_mcp_connection_info. This tool is not exposed to OAuth connectors; use an API key or agent credential whose profile includes it, on a project of the credential's workspace. |
Gotchas:
- A requirement created in the current baseline counts as 'changed' in the working-scope delta; 2+ such changes (or any linked cost, or no linked delivery) make the next publication need a reviewed change set.
- Fires webhook requirement_created and a semantic-embedding sync.
- Retrying creates duplicates - check list_requirements first.
Pairs with: `list_requirement_baselines`, `list_requirement_groups`, `list_requirements`, `get_project_scope_resolution_context`, `create_project_change_set_from_resolution`
CLI: `lpm requirements create --project <projectId> --baseline <baselineId> --title <title> --description <text> --type <type> --status <status> [--group <groupId>] [--source-document <docId>] [--issue <issueId>] [--json]`

### `list_export_requests` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-integrations` · profiles: full, read-only, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the data-export jobs the caller requested, newest first, with their status.
Use when: Polling an export created with create_export_request until it is completed or failed.; Checking whether an export is already queued or running before creating another.    Avoid when: You need the exported data itself: the zip can only be downloaded in the LPM web app (Settings); MCP gives no download link.; You need exports requested by other users: not available.
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| workspaceId | no | list_workspaces -> id | Filter. |
| projectId | no | list_projects -> id | Filter. |
| limitCount | no | constant | Default 20 newest. |
Preconditions: Authenticated caller.
Returns: JSON array sorted by createdAt desc: [{id, scope, workspaceId, projectId, requestedBy, status (queued|running|completed|failed|expired), format 'json-zip', filters, storagePath, signedUrlExpiresAt, recordCounts, checksum (sha256), correlationId, createdAt, updatedAt, completedAt, failedAt, errorMessage}].
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| status 'failed' with errorMessage | Report errorMessage to the user; create a new export only if they ask. |
Gotchas:
- Only exports requested by the caller are returned.
- The response contains no download URL; tell the user to download from LPM Settings.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors.
Pairs with: `create_export_request`, `list_notifications`

### `list_api_keys` [A] · read · KEY · owner `lpm-access` · profiles: full, custom · sensitive: yes · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the caller's own LPM API keys, masked, with profile and status.
Use when: You need keyId for update_api_key or delete_api_key.; Auditing which keys exist, their profile, status and lastUsedAt.; Learning the caller's own userId (field userId).    Avoid when: Workspace owner-agent credentials: use list_workspace_mcp_agent_credentials.; What the current connection can do: use get_mcp_connection_info.
Preconditions: The API key profile is full or custom (sensitive tool).
Returns: JSON array, newest first, of {id, key:'' (always empty), keyPreview ('…' + last 4 chars), name, userId, createdAt, accessProfile, allowedTools (custom only), status (active|revoked), lastUsedAt}.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32003 'This API key is not allowed to call MCP tool: <name>' | Sensitive admin tool: only 'full' or 'custom' API keys include it. Call get_mcp_connection_info and tell the user; never try to widen your own key. |
Gotchas:
- Only the caller's keys.
- The secret is never returned.
- Revoked keys are still listed.
- Not exposed to OAuth connectors (ChatGPT/Claude); needs an API key.
Pairs with: `update_api_key`, `delete_api_key`

### `get_cycle` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-plan-work` · profiles: full, read-only, portfolio, planning, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Returns one cycle with its dates, status and assignee.
Use when: Verify a cycleId or read its dates and status before planning or updating    Avoid when: You need all cycles: list_cycles; You need the cycle's issues: list_issues with cycleId
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id |  |
| cycleId | yes | list_cycles -> id |  |
Preconditions: Caller should have read access to the project; Under OAuth the project must belong to a workspace in the grant
Returns: JSON cycle: id, name, startDate, endDate, status, assigneeId, requirementId, baselineId, projectId, workspaceId, createdAt.
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| -32602 Cycle not found | Wrong cycleId for this project; re-list with list_cycles. |
Pairs with: `list_cycles`, `list_issues`, `update_cycle`

### `list_requirements` [A] · read · portfolio:read · owner `lpm-requirements-scope` · profiles: full, read-only, requirements, custom · sensitive: no · idempotency: naturally idempotent
Purpose: Lists the non-deleted requirements of one baseline with their linked issue/cycle/milestone ids, optionally filtered by group, status or type.
Use when: Reading the approved scope (current baseline) or a past version; Finding a requirementId to update, link or quote; Checking traceability: which requirements have linkedIssueIds    Avoid when: What changed since the baseline - use list_working_scope_delta_entities; Requirements without a baseline - use list_requirements_awaiting_baseline
| Param | Req | Source (call → field) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| projectId | yes | list_projects -> id (or list_workspace_projects -> id) | Firestore project id |
| baselineId | yes | list_requirement_baselines -> id (the isCurrent one) |  |
| groupId | no | list_requirement_groups -> id |  |
| status | no | constant | pending\|met\|not-met\|in-progress\|obsolete |
| type | no | constant | functional\|non-functional\|interface\|business\|technical |
Preconditions: Project exists and the caller can read it
Returns: Array of {id, title, description, type, status, groupId, baselineId, issueId, linkedIssueIds, linkedCycleIds, linkedMilestoneIds, parentRequirementId, dependencies, sourceDocumentId, previousRequirementId, createdAt, updatedAt}
Errors → fix:
| When | Fix |
|---|---|
| Empty array | Wrong baselineId (or empty baseline); take the isCurrent id from list_requirement_baselines. |
| -32003 access denied by OAuth policy, or OPERATION_FAILED under an OAuth connector | Call get_mcp_connection_info to check the portfolio:read scope; OAuth hides domain error text, so retry once and then report the projectId you used. |
Gotchas:
- Not paginated; results over 1 MB are truncated to {items, truncated:true, returned, total, hint} - filter by groupId/status/type.
- Each published baseline has its own requirement copies with new ids (previousRequirementId points to the older copy); use ids from the current baseline.
Pairs with: `list_requirement_baselines`, `update_requirement`, `list_issues`
CLI: `lpm requirements list --project <projectId> --baseline <baselineId> [--status <status>] [--type <type>] [--group <groupId>] [--json]`
